page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance includes four NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, delivering a combined 64 GB of video memory. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, requiring external block storage solutions. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yielded 1103.89, placing it in the bottom 25 percent, while the multi-core CPU test reached 23575.63, falling into the middle 50 percent. Single-threaded gzip compression registered at 19.1 GB/sec, categorized as poor. However, multi-threaded operations show moderate capability, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 112.53 GB/sec and PassMark CPU score at 21092.78. Memory bandwidth write large block is measured at 57.05 GB/sec, and read-only large block is 118.4 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge lies in its architectural generation; the Intel Xeon 8163 processor lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction support, which limits its CPU-based vector and matrix math efficiency. However, the presence of four dedicated NVIDIA V100 GPUs offsets this by offloading parallel computing tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a dense GPU resource allocation relative to its system memory and CPU cores, making it suitable for legacy GPU-accelerated workloads, deep learning training, parallel scientific simulations, and video transcoding rather than CPU-bound single-threaded tasks.
